records.name: Rotation re-mount: invariant features
records.purpose: Do calibration-referenced features change when a sensor is strapped on rotated?
records.assumptions: Rigid sensor, fixed rotation of 2–20° about each sensor axis, same raw stream (virtual re-mount), calibration pose reproduced
records.groundTruth: Identical movement: any difference is a placement artefact
records.metric: largest |Δ| of any invariant feature over all repetitions, sensors, axes and offsets

detail.features: outcome exc_upper_elev exc_fore_elev dur_outbound dur_return peak_rate time_to_peak_fraction sparc_outbound

knownFailureModes: FAILED in the full run (largest 0.196° in 1 of several thousand repetitions; 95th percentile 0.005°): re-quantising the rotated int16 stream can move an onset by one 10 ms sample — see M2a2
does not cover soft-tissue motion or a strap that slips during the recording

records.name: Rotation re-mount: invariant features (post hoc criterion)
records.purpose: As M2a, with one-sample boundary jitter separated from the typical case
records.assumptions: As M2a
records.metric: angles: 95th percentile and largest |Δ| over repetitions; durations: largest |Δ|
records.criterion: angles p95 ≤ 0.01° and max ≤ 0.25°; durations max ≤ 0.01 s (one sample) — POST HOC
knownFailureModes: criterion defined after seeing the M2a result; confirmatory only for later runs

records.name: Rotation re-mount: elbow hinge
records.purpose: How wrong is elbow flexion when the upper-arm sensor is rotated about the bone, and does the stored bound hold?
records.assumptions: Elbow modelled as a hinge about the upper-arm sensor Z axis (core/pipeline.ts); shoulder flexion to ≈ 120°
records.metric: 95th percentile of the elbow excursion error on seeds disjoint from the calibration seeds ÷ stored 95th-percentile table (REATTACHMENT_SENSITIVITY)
records.criterion: ratio ≤ 1.25 at every tabulated offset (the stored table still describes the error)
knownFailureModes: strongly non-linear and heavy-tailed: single repetitions err by 10–20° at a 10–20° rotation
needs many repetitions to estimate: descriptive in quick mode
not evaluated for elbow-flexion tasks with a moving upper arm

records.name: Rotation re-mount: trunk pitch/roll cross-talk
records.purpose: How much pitch appears as roll when the trunk sensor is rotated about the vertical?
records.assumptions: Trunk forward direction taken from the sensor Z axis (mount rule); trunk-assisted repetitions with ≈ 18° of pitch in the set
records.metric: mean |Δ roll excursion| per degree of rotation (slope through the origin, 2–10°)
knownFailureModes: the rotation of the trunk sensor about the vertical cannot be observed from a recording, so this error cannot be detected or bounded per session

records.name: Calibration posture not reproduced
records.purpose: How far does a different arm posture in the calibration pose shift the task outcome?
records.assumptions: Arm held 2–10° forward or sideways during the 3 s calibration, then relaxed; same movement and sensor noise
records.groundTruth: Same movement with the nominal calibration posture
records.metric: bias of the task outcome per degree of posture difference (largest and smallest over movement × direction)
records.criterion: all slopes within [0.8, 1.4] and ≤ the stored bound 1.4
knownFailureModes: posture cannot be told from strap tilt in the recording: the bias is bounded (placement.ts), never corrected
a posture behind the vertical leaves the excursion unchanged but adds to the maximum angle

records.name: Sensor moved along the bone
records.purpose: Does strapping a sensor 2–4 cm further along the segment change the task outcome?
records.assumptions: Rigid segment; only the linear acceleration seen by the accelerometer changes
records.metric: largest |Δ outcome| over repetitions, sensors and shifts
knownFailureModes: faster movements than the simulated ≈ 1.2 s reach raise the centripetal term

records.name: Noise propagation vs independent realisations
records.purpose: Does injecting the stated sensor noise into ONE recording reproduce the spread a feature shows over independent noise realisations?
records.assumptions: White accelerometer (0.004 g) and gyroscope (0.08 °/s) noise per axis; same movement and mount; 12 repetitions per movement seed
records.groundTruth: SD of each repetition feature over 40 independent noise realisations of the same movement, for each of 3 movement seeds
records.metric: share of the seven CORE features whose ratio propagated/true lies in the range for EVERY movement seed (detail: smallest…largest ratio per feature)
records.criterion: every core feature within [0.7, 1.4] and every "approximate" feature within [0.5, 2] (confirmatory, run 3)
knownFailureModes: forearm inclination, outbound duration and forearm onset lag: within a factor of 2 only (flagged "approximate")
elbow flexion: the hinge-branch choice jumps under noise in some movements (ratio 0.03–0.8) — flagged "unstable"
SPARC: injection under-states the spread — flagged "underestimates"
quantised onset lags: conservative

records.name: Systematic budget vs re-mounted sensors
records.purpose: Does the propagated uncertainty of a session mean match how much the mean varies when the sensors are re-mounted (new offsets and biases)?
records.assumptions: Accelerometer zero offset 0.01 g SD, strap misalignment 2–5°, same movement, calibration posture reproduced
records.groundTruth: SD of the recording mean of each feature over 40 re-mounted recordings, for each of 3 movement seeds
records.metric: share of the three core rotation-invariant features with ratio propagated/true in the range for every movement seed
records.criterion: outcome, upper-arm excursion and peak rate within [0.5, 2] (confirmatory, run 3)
knownFailureModes: durations: ratio 0.48–2.01 in earlier runs — at the edge of a factor of 2
trunk roll and elbow flexion vary more than the budget says: their mount sensitivity (M2) is not a sensor-noise term
calibration posture is held fixed here; in practice it adds ≈ 1° per degree (M3)

records.name: Personal envelope: coverage under no change
records.purpose: Does the 95 % envelope contain an unchanged new session 95 % of the time, with few baseline sessions and unequal session lengths?
records.assumptions: Normal repetition (SD 4) and day-to-day (SD 2.5) variation, stationary baseline; a baseline flagged as trending yields no interval
records.groundTruth: New session drawn from the same distribution
records.metric: coverage of the 95 % interval per design (K baseline sessions × n repetitions, new session of m repetitions); value = the coverage furthest from 0.95
knownFailureModes: non-normal or autocorrelated day-to-day variation is not covered
the stability pre-check discards ≈ 5 % of stationary baselines

records.name: Personal envelope: power for a shifted session
records.purpose: How often is a session outside the envelope after a true shift?
records.assumptions: As E1a; the shift is 8 or 15 units (≈ 2.3 or 4.4 SD of a session mean)
records.groundTruth: Shift applied to the new session only
records.metric: share of shifted sessions outside the 95 % envelope
records.criterion: ≥ 0.8 for a 15-unit shift with 5 baseline sessions
knownFailureModes: with 3 baseline sessions the interval is so wide that even a 15-unit shift is usually inside

records.name: Test–retest variance components
records.purpose: Are participant, session and repetition variances recovered without bias from a nested test–retest design?
records.assumptions: 60 participants × 2 occasions × 3 repetitions, normal effects, stable occasions
records.metric: largest relative error of the mean estimated variance over replicates (truncation at 0 biases the session variance upwards in small samples)
knownFailureModes: with ≈ 10 participants the session variance is often estimated as 0 (truncated) or too large: the estimate is unreliable, as its wide CI shows

records.name: Same outcome, different strategy: detection
records.purpose: When two blocks reach the same arm inclination with different trunk involvement, do the profiles differ in the trunk features?
records.assumptions: Arm-dominant vs trunk-assisted repetitions (both ≈ 120° world arm inclination), 12 per block, same sensors on, MPU-6050 noise
records.groundTruth: Strategies differ by 18° of trunk pitch; the task outcome is equal by construction
records.metric: share of replicates where trunk pitch excursion AND trunk contribution are "beyond_noise"
knownFailureModes: a strategy difference in a channel the sensors do not observe (scapula, wrist) is invisible
outcome equivalence needs ≥ ≈ 12 repetitions per block at 6° outcome SD

records.name: Same outcome, different strategy: the outcome is not called different
records.purpose: Is the task outcome falsely reported as changed when only the strategy differs, and are trunk features falsely different when nothing differs?
records.assumptions: As S1a; plus a null comparison of two blocks of the same strategy
records.groundTruth: Equal outcome; identical strategy in the null comparison
records.metric: largest of: share with outcome "beyond_noise"; share of null comparisons with a trunk feature "beyond_noise"
knownFailureModes: per-feature tests at 5 % each: with 15 features about one spurious "beyond_noise" per two comparisons is expected somewhere — only pre-named features should be read

records.name: No change, sensors re-attached
records.purpose: When the movement is unchanged but the sensors are re-attached and the calibration posture is off by 3–8°, is a change of the movement reported?
records.assumptions: Identical movement plan in both sessions; new strap misalignment, offsets and biases; arm held 3–8° forward in the second calibration
records.groundTruth: No change of the movement; the measured outcome shifts by about the posture error
records.metric: largest of: share where the outcome difference is "beyond_noise" (not attributed to placement); share where 4 re-attached sessions are said to exceed measurement explanations
knownFailureModes: run 1 failed (12.5 %): strap tilt and posture cancelled in the calibration direction; a 5° strap allowance was added to the attribution bound (provisional)
the guard works by REFUSING to attribute: a real change smaller than ≈ 7° + 1.4 × the tilt difference between two sessions is also reported as "within_placement"
a posture error that leaves the calibration tilt unchanged (e.g. compensated by strap tilt) is not flagged

records.name: Flexibility index: no false adaptation under pure scaling
records.purpose: If the child reaches a higher target with the SAME organisation scaled up, is "condition-dependent organisation" reported?
records.assumptions: Two target heights interleaved in one session, 12 repetitions each; the low-target movement is the high-target movement at 75 % amplitude; share curves
records.metric: share of replicates with verdict condition_dependent_organisation
knownFailureModes: forearm inclination and elbow flexion are excluded: their dynamic error grows with speed² and faked adaptation in 3 of 8 development sessions
a fixed (non-scaling) movement component, e.g. a constant trunk sway, makes shares differ between amplitudes and is read as adaptation
timing differences between conditions survive landmark registration only partly

records.name: Flexibility index: power for a real change of organisation
records.purpose: If the low target is reached with the arm alone and the high target with trunk assistance, is it detected?
records.assumptions: As S3a; low target arm-only (0° trunk), high target trunk-assisted (18° trunk)
records.metric: share of replicates with verdict condition_dependent_organisation
knownFailureModes: conditions recorded in different sessions are refused (confounded with re-attachment) however large the difference

records.name: Trunk–outcome trade-off: recovery of the pass-through
records.purpose: Is the share of trunk variation that passes into the task outcome recovered when the arm fully compensates (0) and when it does not (1)?
records.assumptions: Sagittal arm raising, 24 repetitions, trunk pitch SD 5°; planar chain outcome = arm relative to trunk − trunk pitch; trunk noise 0.04°
records.groundTruth: pass-through 0 (shoulder = 120° + pitch) and 1 (shoulder independent of pitch)
records.metric: largest |mean estimated pass-through − truth| over the two designs
knownFailureModes: out-of-plane arm movement breaks the planar model (refused below planarity 0.9)
if the trunk barely varies the slope is undefined (refused below 1° SD)
a common drive (both trunk and arm larger on "effortful" repetitions) is read as pass-through > 1, not as compensation

records.name: Movement signature: identification across re-attached sessions
records.purpose: Is a participant's second session matched to their own first session when participants differ in their movement organisation?
records.assumptions: 8 synthetic participants with individual shoulder/trunk/elbow amplitudes, trunk timing and speed; 2 sessions × 8 repetitions; sensors re-attached between sessions
records.groundTruth: Each participant has their own generating parameters
records.metric: mean identification rate (chance = 1 / participants)
knownFailureModes: synthetic participants differ far more cleanly than real children; real identification is unknown
features sensitive to placement (elbow, trunk roll) would masquerade as signature if a participant always wore the sensors the same wrong way

records.name: Movement signature: no signature when participants do not differ
records.purpose: Is a signature reported when every participant moves by the same generating parameters?
records.assumptions: 8 participants with identical parameters; only repetition variability and re-attachment differ
records.metric: share of replicates with verdict reproducible_signature

records.name: Strategy shift: false alarms under a stable mixture
records.purpose: With one stable 50/50 mixture of two strategies over 5 sessions, how often is a shift reported?
records.assumptions: 5 sessions × 10 confidently assigned repetitions, independent assignments
records.metric: share of replicates with verdict shift_detected
knownFailureModes: assignments within a session are not independent if strategies persist in runs: the permutation is then anti-conservative

records.name: Strategy shift: power for a switch
records.purpose: Is a change of the share from 0.2 to 0.8 between sessions 2 and 3 detected?
records.assumptions: As S6a
records.metric: share of replicates with verdict shift_detected
knownFailureModes: a single split describes a gradual change poorly: power is lower and the split position is not meaningful

records.name: Change detection: false alarms under no change
records.purpose: How often does the primary detector signal a change in a series that has none, when the level and spread are learned from the series itself?
records.assumptions: Independent normal session means, no change; 10 or 20 sessions; self-starting residuals
records.metric: largest series-wise false-alarm probability of the CUSUM over the two horizons
knownFailureModes: autocorrelated or heavy-tailed day-to-day variation (O4, O5)
series longer than the design horizon

records.name: Change detection: power and delay for a step
records.purpose: How large must a lasting change of level be, and how many sessions does it take, before it is signalled?
records.assumptions: 20 sessions, step after session 8, in units of the day-to-day SD of a session mean
records.metric: power for a 2 SD step (alarm at or after the change)
knownFailureModes: a self-starting chart absorbs an undetected shift into its own mean and spread: small steps are missed permanently
with 10 sessions and a change after the 4th the power is low — "no signal" is not evidence of stability

records.name: Change detection: missing sessions
records.purpose: Do missing sessions create false alarms, and how much do they hide a real decline — especially when poor sessions are the ones that go missing?
records.assumptions: 20 planned sessions; 30 % missing at random, or sessions more than 0.5 SD below the starting level missed with probability 0.6; nothing is interpolated
records.groundTruth: No change, or a decline of 2 SD after session 8
records.metric: false-alarm probability with 30 % of sessions missing at random
knownFailureModes: sessions missed BECAUSE performance was poor hide a decline: the power falls and nothing in the data reveals it — the reason for a missed session must be recorded

records.name: Change detection: autocorrelated day-to-day variation
records.purpose: What happens to the false-alarm probability when consecutive sessions are correlated (AR(1), ρ = 0.5) — a violation of the detector's assumption?
records.assumptions: Stationary AR(1) session means, ρ = 0.5, no change of level
records.metric: false-alarm probability of the CUSUM
knownFailureModes: slowly wandering performance is signalled as a change far more often than 5 %: a signal says "not one stable level", which a slow wander is not either

records.name: Change detection: heavy-tailed session noise
records.purpose: What happens to the false-alarm probability when single sessions are occasionally far off (Student-t, 3 df)?
records.assumptions: Independent t(3) session deviations scaled to unit variance, no change of level
records.metric: false-alarm probability of the CUSUM
knownFailureModes: an outlying session early in the series inflates the running SD and reduces power afterwards

records.name: Bayesian change point: calibration and position
records.purpose: Is strong posterior support for a change rare when there is none, and is the position of a real change recovered?
records.assumptions: 16 independent normal sessions; prior probability ½ of a change, uniform over its position, standardised shift ~ N(0, 1)
records.groundTruth: No change, or a 2 SD step after session 8
records.metric: share of unchanged series with posterior probability of a change ≥ 0.9; share of changed series with the most likely position within ±1 session
knownFailureModes: the posterior depends on the prior scale of the shift: it is always reported at three scales
a single change is assumed: a gradual change is described as a step somewhere in the middle

records.name: Change detection: five features monitored together
records.purpose: When five features of the same sessions are monitored, is the chance of ANY false alarm still about 5 %?
records.assumptions: Five independent unchanged series of 20 sessions; thresholds for α/5
records.metric: probability that at least one of the five signals
knownFailureModes: real features are positively correlated: the correction is then conservative (less power), not wrong

records.name: Change detection: gradual drift
records.purpose: Is a slow, steady change (0.2 SD per session from session 6) signalled, and when?
records.assumptions: 20 sessions; linear drift reaching 2.8 SD at the last session
records.metric: probability of a signal
knownFailureModes: a self-starting chart partly learns a slow drift as part of the normal spread

records.name: Change detection: a step caused by measurement conditions
records.purpose: If the sensor-placement protocol changes at session 10 and shifts the metric by 1.5 SD, does the detector signal it?
records.assumptions: The movement does not change; a constant measurement bias of 1.5 SD from session 10 (e.g. a different operator or strap position)
records.metric: probability of a signal
knownFailureModes: the detector cannot tell a change of measurement conditions from a change of the movement: every signal must be checked against placement confidence and the session log before it is interpreted (lab/discovery/explanations.ts)

records.name: Within-session pattern: none
records.purpose: With no change across the repetitions of a sitting, how often is a pattern reported?
records.assumptions: 24 repetitions, four independent features, normal repetition noise
records.metric: share of sittings with any pattern other than no_trend_detected
knownFailureModes: run 1 failed (12.1 %): shapes were chosen by AICc alone; a permutation test per feature, Holm-adjusted, now decides whether a feature moves
features of one movement are correlated; the Holm correction assumes nothing about that and stays valid

records.name: Within-session pattern: practice-like
records.purpose: Is a steady improvement of 2 repetition-SDs across a sitting recognised?
records.assumptions: 24 repetitions; every feature moves 2 SD in the "up" direction, linearly
records.metric: share classified practice_like
knownFailureModes: with 8–12 repetitions the power is much lower

records.name: Within-session pattern: decline-like
records.purpose: Is a steady decline of 2 repetition-SDs across a sitting recognised — and reported as a pattern, not as fatigue?
records.assumptions: As W2, in the "down" direction
records.metric: share classified decline_like
knownFailureModes: fatigue, loss of attention, discomfort and boredom give the same pattern

records.name: Within-session pattern: rise then decline
records.purpose: Is an improvement followed by a decline (2.5 SD up over the first half, back down over the second) recognised?
records.assumptions: 30 repetitions, symmetric rise and fall in every feature
records.groundTruth: Rise then decline, slope change at the middle
records.metric: share classified rise_then_decline
knownFailureModes: a rise and fall of equal size has no linear trend: with fewer than 12 repetitions it is reported as no trend

records.name: Population model: parameter recovery
records.purpose: Does the EM fit of the random-intercept-and-slope model recover the mean change, the spread of individual levels and slopes, and the residual SD?
records.assumptions: 40 participants × 8 weekly sessions; normal random effects (SD 10 and 0.8/week, correlation −0.2), residual SD 3
records.groundTruth: β = (100, 1.5), D and σ as stated
records.metric: largest relative error of the mean estimate over replicates (ML variance estimates are biased low by ≈ 1/participants)
knownFailureModes: with ≈ 10 participants the slope variance is poorly determined
non-linear individual trajectories are forced onto lines (T2b)

records.name: Held-out participants, future sessions: calibration
records.purpose: For a participant the model has never seen, are sessions 4–10 predicted from sessions 1–3 with calibrated 95 % intervals, and better than without the population?
records.assumptions: 30 participants × 10 weekly sessions; leave-one-participant-out; own sessions 1–3 given; linear truth
records.groundTruth: Simulated future sessions of the held-out participant
records.metric: coverage of the 95 % prediction intervals over all held-out future observations
records.criterion: coverage within [0.9, 0.98], calibration slope within [0.85, 1.15], MAE below the individual-only line
knownFailureModes: only valid for participants exchangeable with the sample the model was fitted on
synthetic participants: says nothing about real children

records.name: Held-out participants, future sessions: misspecified shape
records.purpose: What happens to the same predictions when individual trajectories level off but the model assumes straight lines?
records.assumptions: 30 participants × 10 weekly sessions; leave-one-participant-out; own sessions 1–3 given; saturating truth (time constant 4 weeks)
records.groundTruth: Simulated future sessions of the held-out participant
records.metric: coverage of the 95 % prediction intervals over all held-out future observations
knownFailureModes: a linear population model extrapolates a saturating child upwards: intervals under-cover late sessions

records.name: Prediction engine: coverage of issued intervals
records.purpose: Do the model-averaged 95 % intervals for the next session contain it about 95 % of the time, whatever the true shape — and is a forecast refused when there is too little data?
records.assumptions: 10 weekly sessions × 3 repetitions (σε 4, σs 2.5), next session one week later; truth stationary, linear or exponential
records.metric: coverage of the 95 % interval over all issued predictions
knownFailureModes: coverage is conditional on the day-to-day variation staying as it was
refusals remove the hardest cases from the coverage figure — the refusal rates are part of the result

records.name: Identifiability is detected, not hidden
records.purpose: When two parameters or two explanations cannot be told apart from the data, does the analysis say so instead of reporting precise-looking values?
records.assumptions: (a) learning with forgetting on a regular weekly schedule with constant dose; (b) a slow exponential curve (τ = 60 d) observed for 8 weekly sessions
records.groundTruth: (a) forgetting and saturation are confounded by design; (b) the time constant is not bounded by 8 weeks of data
records.metric: share of (a) flagged "confounded_by_schedule"; share of (b) with an open profile interval for the time constant
records.criterion: (a) = 1; (b) ≥ 0.6; no selected model with an open interval without a warning
knownFailureModes: profile likelihood detects parameters the data do not bound; it does not detect a wrong model form

records.name: Learning with forgetting: retention kept apart from performance
records.purpose: With known learning, a no-practice interval and a designated retention session, are immediate performance and the retained change represented separately, and is the forgetting half-life recovered with honest uncertainty?
records.assumptions: Single-rate learning with forgetting (half-life 21 d, gain 0.3 units/min), 10 sessions × 5 repetitions, varying dose, breaks of 4 and 6 weeks, practice log available
records.groundTruth: half-life 21 d; true retention ratio after the 6-week break 0.25
records.metric: coverage of the true half-life by the 95 % profile interval; share of runs in which the designated session is a retention test without recorded practice
knownFailureModes: the retention ratio of ONE session pair is noisy (session noise in numerator and denominator)
"no practice in the delay" comes from the practice log: reported, not observed

records.name: Scenario 1: No actual motor change
records.purpose: No change signalled; "no change" selected
records.assumptions: Constant latent level; day-to-day SD 2.5, repetition SD 4, 12 weekly sessions × 3 repetitions. Simplification: independent normal day-to-day variation
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: independent normal day-to-day variation

records.name: Scenario 2: True movement improvement
records.purpose: A model of change selected, or a change signalled
records.assumptions: Linear increase of 2 units per week over 12 weekly sessions. Simplification: a perfectly linear trend
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: a perfectly linear trend

records.name: Scenario 3: True coordination change at equal outcome
records.purpose: The trunk onset lag differs beyond noise; the outcome does not
records.assumptions: Two blocks of 12 repetitions, same sensors on: trunk starts 100 ms after the arm, then 350 ms BEFORE it (and moves 20 % faster); planned joint amplitudes identical. Simplification: two discrete timing patterns, minimum-jerk profiles. Two properties of the MEASUREMENT, found when the scenario was built (80 seeds): the measured lag shift is about −190 ms, not the planned −450 ms, because the arm sensor is carried by the trunk and so "starts" with it; and the measured peak is about 0.7° lower in the second pattern, because the trunk has begun to return when the arm peaks — smaller than the repetition noise of a 12-repetition block
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: two discrete timing patterns, minimum-jerk profiles. Two properties of the MEASUREMENT, found when the scenario was built (80 seeds): the measured lag shift is about −190 ms, not the planned −450 ms, because the arm sensor is carried by the trunk and so "starts" with it; and the measured peak is about 0.7° lower in the second pattern, because the trunk has begun to return when the arm peaks — smaller than the repetition noise of a 12-repetition block

records.name: Scenario 4: Strategy transition across sessions
records.purpose: A shift is detected
records.assumptions: Share of strategy A among confident assignments 0.2, 0.2, 0.8, 0.8, 0.8 over five sessions of 10 repetitions. Simplification: independent assignments within a session
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: independent assignments within a session

records.name: Scenario 5: Trunk contribution increases while the outcome stays
records.purpose: Change in the trunk series, none in the outcome series — reported as a change of contribution, never as better or worse
records.assumptions: Session mean of the trunk excursion rises by 1.5° per week over 12 sessions; the task outcome is constant. Simplification: session-level series of two features generated independently
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: session-level series of two features generated independently

records.name: Scenario 6: Trunk contribution decreases while the outcome stays
records.purpose: Change in the trunk series, none in the outcome series — reported as a change of contribution, never as better or worse
records.assumptions: Session mean of the trunk excursion falls by 1.5° per week over 12 sessions; the task outcome is constant. Simplification: session-level series of two features generated independently
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: session-level series of two features generated independently

records.name: Scenario 7: Sensor re-attachment, no change
records.purpose: The outcome shift is NOT reported as a change of the movement
records.assumptions: The same movement plan recorded twice; new strap misalignment, offsets and biases; arm held 3–8° forward in the second calibration. Simplification: posture error in one direction only; rigid straps
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: posture error in one direction only; rigid straps

records.name: Scenario 8: Gyroscope drift
records.purpose: The task outcome stays within 3° of the kinematic truth, and no repetition is lost silently
records.assumptions: Gyroscope bias random walk of 0.05 °/s per √s after calibration. Simplification: bias random walk only
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: bias random walk only

records.name: Scenario 9: Accelerometer and gyroscope noise ×6
records.purpose: The task outcome stays within 3° of the kinematic truth, and no repetition is lost silently
records.assumptions: Sensor noise six times the nominal MPU-6050 level. Simplification: white noise only
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: white noise only

records.name: Scenario 10: Missing packets
records.purpose: Signal quality is downgraded; repetitions with missing samples are excluded with a reason, never interpolated
records.assumptions: 5 % of frames dropped independently after calibration. Simplification: independent drops, no bursts
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: independent drops, no bursts

records.name: Scenario 11: Sensor dropout (trunk sensor absent)
records.purpose: Trunk channels are reported unavailable; no trunk value is produced
records.assumptions: Trunk-assisted repetitions recorded WITHOUT the trunk sensor. Simplification: sensor absent for the whole recording
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: sensor absent for the whole recording

records.name: Scenario 12: Task-condition change between sessions
records.purpose: The sessions are declared not comparable and the difference is attributed to the task condition
records.assumptions: Sessions 1–3 to a 90° target, sessions 4–6 to a 120° target; the child does exactly what each target asks. Simplification: no other difference between the conditions
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: no other difference between the conditions

records.name: Scenario 13: Fatigue-like within-session deterioration
records.purpose: Pattern "decline_like" — a kinematic pattern, not a diagnosis of fatigue
records.assumptions: 24 repetitions; amplitude, peak rate, duration and smoothness move 2 repetition-SDs in the "down" direction, linearly. Simplification: all features move together and linearly
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: all features move together and linearly

records.name: Scenario 14: Practice-related within-session improvement
records.purpose: Pattern "practice_like" — a kinematic pattern, not a diagnosis of learning
records.assumptions: 24 repetitions; amplitude, peak rate, duration and smoothness move 2 repetition-SDs in the "up" direction, linearly. Simplification: all features move together and linearly
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do
knownFailureModes: all features move together and linearly

records.name: Scenario 15: Between-session retention
records.purpose: The designated session after the 6-week break is recognised as a retention test without recorded practice
records.assumptions: Single-rate learning with forgetting: baseline 80, half-life 21 d, gain 0.3 per minute; 10 sessions × 5 repetitions, breaks of 4 and 6 weeks, practice log. Simplification: one exponential forgetting rate; practice reported exactly
records.metric: share of runs in which the engine did what a correct analysis must do

records.name: Holm: family-wise error over ten true nulls
records.purpose: When ten features are tested and none has changed, how often is at least one called changed — with and without adjustment?
records.assumptions: Ten independent two-sided z-tests, all null
records.metric: probability of at least one rejection after Holm adjustment
knownFailureModes: controls errors only within the declared family: features examined but not reported are outside it

records.name: Benjamini–Hochberg: false discovery rate with real effects present
records.purpose: When 5 of 20 features truly changed, what share of the reported changes is false?
records.assumptions: 20 independent z-tests, 5 with a 3 SE effect
records.metric: mean false discovery proportion at q = 0.05
knownFailureModes: valid for independent or positively dependent tests
